doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Thelonious Monk, Hall Overton and the big-band arrangements
summary: Overton's arrangements caught Monk's spirit and rehearsals at Sixth Avenue.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Wow. Interesting. And then Thelonious Monk.

Well I think Hall Overton did a fantastic job writing that music because he caught the spirit. He got it right. He used to be playing piano, you know, when we were rehearsing, at Sixth Avenue around 28th Street on the second floor. There was a lot going on there. But he used to play the piano and Monk would be in the other room dancing. And he’d say, “but when are you going to play the piano?” He said, “when the tempo gets right.” Yeah those rehearsals were something.
Wow. You have worked with some characters.
Here’s a piece I hope — whoops, I think I went the wrong way — from about that time.
Now – that’s good stuff. It’s interesting when you say that Hall Overton caught the spirit. Because those [scats] those dissonances in there, would Monk have told him to do that?

I have no idea what Monk told him. But whatever he did —because you can’t write like what could I say — normal — you’ve got to write like Monk played it. And he don’t play all the notes in the chord. You know he just plays specific notes. That’s how he gets that sound. And you’ve got to know which ones to leave out. Otherwise it don’t sound like Monk at all.
